faqs.a: GSTIN is 15 characters: 2-digit state code + 10-character PAN + 1 entity digit + Z + 1 check digit. For example, 07ABCPE1234F1ZD breaks into 07 (Delhi), ABCPE1234F (PAN), 1 (entity), Z, D (check).
faqs.q: What is the structure of a GSTIN?

faqs.a: The first two digits are the state code where the business is registered: 27 is Maharashtra, 07 is Delhi, 29 is Karnataka, 09 is Uttar Pradesh. This validator recognizes all 36 active GST state codes.
faqs.q: What do the first two digits of GSTIN mean?

faqs.a: The 15th character is a check digit computed from the first 14 using a mod-36 algorithm. Change any earlier character and the check digit stops matching, which is how typos get caught.
faqs.q: What is the check digit in GSTIN?

faqs.a: No. It proves the number is well-formed, not that it is registered. The only real confirmation is the GST portal's search, which this offline tool cannot reach.
faqs.q: Does a valid GSTIN mean the business is registered?

faqs.a: Usually a typo in the PAN portion or the state code. Double-check against the registration certificate. If the check digit fails but everything else looks right, one character is wrong - retype carefully.
faqs.q: Why does my GSTIN fail the checksum?

faqs.a: Yes. Regular taxpayers get a 15-character GSTIN. UIN holders and some special entities have different formats that this validator does not cover - see the GST portal for those.

gstin-validator.formula:
GSTIN structure (15 characters):
Positions 1-2: state code (01-38, valid codes only)
Positions 3-12: PAN of the holder (AAAAA9999A, valid holder code)
Position 13: entity number (0-9, A-Z)
Position 14: always Z
Position 15: check digit (mod-36 of first 14 chars)
Check: value = (36 - (sum mod 36)) mod 36, digits 0-9 = 0-9, letters A-Z = 10-35.
howTo: Type or paste the 15-character GSTIN into the input box.
The validator checks it live: length, pattern, state code, PAN holder code, and check digit.
A green message with the breakdown means the GSTIN is structurally valid.
A red message tells you exactly which check failed.
keyFacts: A GSTIN is exactly 15 characters long.
The first two digits are the GST state code, from 01 to 38.
Characters 3-12 are the PAN of the business or person.
Character 14 is always the letter Z.
The 15th character is a mod-36 check digit computed from the first 14.
Structure alone never proves registration - only the GST portal can confirm that.

reasons.checksum: The check digit does not match - at least one character is wrong.

reasons.panHolder: The PAN portion has an invalid holder code at its 4th character.
reasons.pattern: GSTIN must follow the pattern: 2 digits, PAN, entity digit, Z, check digit.
reasons.state: The first two digits are not a valid GST state code.

2. Pattern: 07 + ABCPE1234F + 1 + Z + D matches the GSTIN layout.
